newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's rates Toshiba MTN programme A1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Toshiba MTN programme A1.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had assigned an A1 senior unsecured debt rating to the $1 billion Euro Medium-Term Note (MTN) Programme of Toshiba Corp and an affiliate, Toshiba International Finance (Netherlands) BV.

Moody's said in a statement that the rating was based on Toshiba's leading-edge technologies and strong market position in its core business. It also incorporated Moody's expectation that Toshiba would continue to face severe operating environments and strong global competition in most of its core businesses over the intermediate term.

Moody's said it expects pricing of memory devices to recover from the low experienced in the past 12 to 18 months, but that global over-capacity would continue to result in cyclical pricing and weakened cash flows.

It added that industry participants would face ever higher costs for research and development and capital expenditure, which could increase the financial risk profile during a downturn in the semiconductor market.

Toshiba has a leading position in the U.S. market for notebook personal computers and is having some success in enhancing market share in the domestic market with unique products, it said. But Moody's said extremely keen price competition would put pressure on Toshiba's PC profit margins.
It said Toshiba's consumer electronics division, suffering from market maturation and severe competition, was improving, but the division's profitability may remain weak.

Moody's said that overall it expects Toshiba's operating performance to improve but to be below its historical levels for the near- to medium-term. But it said Toshiba's established market positions and its excellent technological strengths should provide sufficient predictability of earnings and cash flows to support its A1 long-term rating.
